observations: The component renders only text links (a title and a list of anchor links); it contains no images, icons, or other non-text content requiring a text alternative.

standard: 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (Level A)

observations: The component renders a heading (when `title` is set) followed by a semantic unordered list of links; the list/item/link relationships are conveyed programmatically by the markup itself, not left to the implementer.
The component has no form inputs.
Hover/active/focus states are reinforced by a background-color change and a leading stripe accent, but link text itself is always visible and is never conveyed by color alone.
Title and link text colors are drawn from CivicTheme's heading/body color tokens against the component's background tokens, meeting the minimum 4.5:1 ratio in both light and dark themes.
Text uses relative (rem) units throughout, so it remains visible and readable when resized to at least 200%.
All text (title and links) is rendered as real text; the component has no image-of-text rendering path.
The focus-visible outline and the link's leading stripe accent are drawn from the shared outline/border tokens, which meet the 3:1 minimum contrast against adjacent colors in both themes.
Text remains visible/readable when line spacing, letter spacing, and word spacing are adjusted to the SC 1.4.12 minimums; no fixed-height container clips overflowing text.

standard: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA)
observations: Hover/focus only change background/stripe color; no additional content is revealed.
Every link is a native <a> element, so all links are reachable and operable using the keyboard alone.
Simple native links with no scripted focus management; keyboard focus can always move away.

standard: 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

observations: This component links to sections within the current page; it is not a mechanism for bypassing blocks of content repeated across multiple pages (the SC's actual subject), so it does not itself satisfy 2.4.1 even though it aids in-page navigation.
Links receive focus in the same order as their `ct-table-of-contents-item` children are declared, which matches the rendered visual order.
Compliance depends on the implementer providing link text (each item's `label`) that clearly identifies the target section, rather than generic text like "click here" or "more".
SC 2.4.5 concerns locating a Web page within a set of Web pages, not navigating within a single page's sections, so this in-page link list does not itself satisfy it.
Compliance depends on the implementer providing a clear, descriptive `title` (e.g. "On this page") and descriptive per-item `label` text.
Links have an explicit `:focus-visible` outline (offset/width/color from the shared outline tokens) in both light and dark themes.
The component has no accessible-name override mechanism (no `aria-label` prop); each link's accessible name is always its own visible text, so there is no case where a mismatch could occur.

Each link is a block-level element with 0.5rem vertical padding around 1.25rem line-height text (~36px computed height) plus 1rem/1.25rem horizontal padding, comfortably exceeding the 24x24 CSS pixel minimum.
Compliance depends on the implementer setting the correct `lang` attribute on the surrounding page's html element.
Compliance depends on the implementer setting a `lang` attribute on a link's text if it differs from the page's main language.
Focusing a link triggers no context change; navigation only occurs on activation, matching standard link behavior.
The component has no input controls that could trigger an unexpected context change.
Where a table of contents is used across a set of pages, it is presented in the same relative position and structure each time.
The component is rendered and labelled consistently every time it is used (same title/link markup structure).
The component has no form inputs or validation to identify errors on.
The component has no form inputs requiring labels or instructions.
The component has no form inputs that can produce validation errors.
Links are native <a> elements, so their name (visible text), role (link), and value (href) are exposed to assistive technologies without any additional ARIA authoring.
The component is static once rendered; it makes no dynamic status announcements.
